Krishan Kumar vs Food Safety Officer on 20 March, 2023 In The Court Of Mr. Dharmesh Sharma Principal District & Sessions Judge / Food Safety Appellate Tribunal; New Delhi District Patiala House Courts : New Delhi Fsat No. 11/2021 Cnr No. Dlnd010083312021 1. Ahuja, Advocate for appellant. Sh. Manoj Kr. Dubey, Ld. Chief Pp for State/respondent. Judgment:
texts.facts: FACTUAL BACKGROUND: 2. Briefly stated, it is the case of the appellants that Sh. Shrey Kumar S/o Sh. Krishan Kumar is the Authorised representative appellant No. 3 company viz., M/s Aadvik Foods and Products Pvt. Ltd. whereas Sh. Hitesh Rathi is the nominee and Sh. Rakesh H. Thakkar is the nominee of appellant no.5 M/s Ruchi Foods LLP, having its registered office at Ground Floor, Piyush Cottage, Parabia Compound, Opp Express Hotel Alkapuri, Vadodara, Gujarat - 390007, which incidentally is the manufacturer of the food item. It is stated that Sh. Naresh Kumar Sharma, Food Safety Officer (in short "FSO") on 06.07.2020 took a sample of "Camel Milk Powder" for analysis from the Food Business OperatorcumDirector Sh. Shrey Kumar S/o Sh. Krishan Kumar (in short "FBO") from the premises of appellant no.3 company M/s Aadvik Foods and Products Pvt. Ltd. situated at 2 nd Floor, Plot No. 475, Patparganj Industrial Area, New Delhi110092, where the said food article was stored for sale for human consumption; and that the sample consisted of 8 packets each 150 kg sealed packets in original condition with identical batch number and label declaration, each stated to be containing "Camel Milk Powder"; and that each packet was separately marked, packed, fastened and sealed by the FSO, for which a payment of Rs.5,200/ was paid in terms of notice in the prescribed Form VA towards cost of the 08 nos. of packets; and notice in Form VA in terms of 2.4.1(4) of FSS Rules, 2011 was prepared and sent to appellant no.5. 3. As per the predictable drill, one counter part of the sample of "Camel Milk Powder" bearing sample number 336/1054/73/2020 with Designated Officer Code Number 03/DO25/21258 was sent by the applicant/FSO to the Food Analyst for analysis for 07.07.2020 but no request was received from the FBO to send the 4 th counter part of the sample for analysis by NABL accredited Laboratory under Rule 2.4.5 of FSS Rules, 2011. Anyhow, it is further stated that Food Analyst vide his report no. FSS/795/2020 dated 17.07.2020 has declared that the label as "Percentage of cocoa solids not declared in the lists of ingredients although it is emphasized as present on the label through graphics"; and that" best before declaration" on label is not given in capital letter" and that the Food Analyst in the aforesaid report also opined that the sample was misbranded for violation of Regulation No. 2.2.2.2(f)(i) and 2.2.2.10 of the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging & Labelling) Regulation, 2011 (hereinafter referred as FSS (P&L) Regulation) and 2.12.1.3 of the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standard & Food Additives) Regulation, 2011 (hereinafter referred as FSS (FPS&FA) Regulation). 4. It is also a matter of record that the Designated Officer (East) sent a copy of the Food Analyst Report along with forwarding letter dated 28.07.2020 to the FBOcumDirector Sh. Shrey Kumar as also to the suppliercummanufacturing firm viz. Appellant no.5 to afford them an opportunity to file an appeal against the report of the Food Analyst under Section 46(4) of the FSS Act for sending one part of the sample to the Referral Food Laboratory, if so desired, but none has preferred Sh. Shrey Kumar S/O Sh. Krishan Kumar vs Food Safety Officer on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13925913/ 2 to file an appeal against the report of the Food Analyst. It is also a matter of record that the food article i.e. "Camel Milk Powder" was manufactured, packed or further supplied by appellant no. 5 M/s Ruchi Foods LLP, to appellant no.3 company viz. M/s Aadvik Foods and Products Pvt. Ltd., vide invoice dated 04.06.2020 and appellant no.4 Sh. Rakesh H. Thakkar was the Incharge and responsible for the conduct and daytoday business of appellant no. 5 M/s Ruchi Foods LLP. 5. Suffice to state that notices were issued to the parties by the Ld. AO/ADM and after hearing the parties, the impugned order was passed by the Ld. AO/ADM, the operative part of which goes as under : "14. The above said accused/ respondents violating the provision of Section 23 (1) and Section 26(1) & 26 (2) (ii), Section 27(2)(c) read with Section 3(1)(zf) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and violated Regulation No. 2.2.2.2 (f)(i) and 2.2.2.10 of The Food Safety and Standards (Packaging & Labelling) Regulation, 2011 and also violated Regulation no. 2.12.1.3 of the Food Safety & Standards (Food Products Standards & Food Additives) Regulation, 2011 which is punishable U/s 52 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. As per the section 52 in The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, any person who whether by himself or by any other person on his behalf manufactures for sale or stores or sells or distributes or imports any article of food for human consumption which is misbranded, shall be liable to a penalty which may extend to three lakh rupees. 15. Keeping in view of the above facts and circumstances, and also the accused have admitted the previous mistakes in their reply. Hence, in this case is decided in view of Section 52 of Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 read with section 49, there is laid down criteria of adjudging to impose the penalty like the amount of gain, unfair advantage, amount of loss caused, likely to cause, repetitive nature of contravention etc. It is contravention of provisions of FSS Act, 2006 by the above named respondents. The undersigned is of the considered view, that a penalty of Rs. 1,50,000/ (Rupees One Lakh Fifty Thousand Only) is imposed upon Respondent No. 1 i.e. Sh. Shrey Kumar who is FBOcumDirectorcumNominee of Accused No. 3, a penalty of Rs. 1,50,000/ (Rupees One Lakh Fifty Thousand Only) is imposed upon respondent no. 2 i.e Sh. Hitesh Rathi who is Director cumNominee of Accused No. 3, a penalty of Rs. 1,00,000/ (Rupees One Lakh Only) is imposed upon respondent no. 3 i.e. M/s Aadvik Foods and Products Pvt Ltd, a penalty of Rs. 1,00,000/ (Rupees One Lakh Only) is imposed upon respondent no. 4 i.e. Sh. Rakesh H. Thakkar (Nominee of Accused No.5) , a penalty of Rs.2,00,000/ (Rupees Two Lakh Only) is imposed upon respondent no.5 i.e M/s. Ruchi Foods LLP which is manufacturingcumpacking unit and also supplier to accused No.3 i.e.M/s. Aadvik Foods and Products Pvt. Ltd. GROUNDS OF APPEAL: Sh. Shrey Kumar S/O Sh. Krishan Kumar vs Food Safety Officer on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13925913/ 3 6. Hence, relief is sought to quash the impugned order dated 27.10.2021 passed by the Ld. AO/ADM. 8. On the filing of the present appeal, the same was admitted for hearing subject to the appellants furnishing demand draft/FDR equivalent to the 50% of the fine/penalty imposed upon them, and consequently, FDR in the sum of Rs. 3.5 lakhs has been submitted by way of demand draft, drawn on HDFC Bank, Patparganj, New Delhi, dated 08.12.2021. Notice of the present appeal was issued to the respondent, who have entered appearance and the original record of Ld. Adjudicating Officer is produced. Although, no reply is filed, the appeal is opposed.
texts.arguments: The term 'proprietary item' is defined by Regulation 2.12 of the FSS (FPS&FA) Regulation), which reads as under: "2.12 PROPRIETARY FOOD [2.12.1: For the purpose of these regulations, (1) Proprietary food means an article of food that has not been standardised under these regulations, but does not include novel foods, foods for special dietary uses, foods for special medical purposes, functional foods, nutraceuticals, health supplements and such other food articles which the Central Government may notify in this behalf: Provided that any deviation in quality parameters of a standardised food, as specified in the Food Safety and Standards Regulations made under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 shall not qualify the resultant product as a proprietary food. (2) Proprietary food shall contain only those ingredients other than additives which are either standardised or permitted for use in the preparation of other standardised food under these Regulations, except the ingredients which may be specified by the Authority from time to time. (3) Proprietary food shall use only such additives and at such levels, as specified for the Category or Subcategory under Appendix A of these Regulations, to which the food belongs. 14. Secondly, the decision as regards violation of Regulation 2.2.2.10 of the FSS (P&L) Regulation about 'nondeclaration of best before/expiry not being in capital letters' was a trivial infringement of the Regulation that was also not actionable in view of decision in the case Pramod Kumar Kedia v. State of Bihar (supra); Oscar Joseph & Anr v State of Jharkhand & Ors and M.D. Anand Aqua M/s S.N.B. Industries v State of Bihar & Anr (supra), wherein it was categorically held that even writing 'best before statement' in small letters was sufficient compliance for regulation 2.2.2 (10) of the FSS (Labelling and Packaging) Regulations, 2011.
